findings.title: V2 canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the Groups resource-type resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() checks via auth.groups().requireManage(), so an admin who was only granted the `view` scope on all groups can create top-level groups in the realm. This is a privilege escalation; the check should only accept AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (mirroring canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks MANAGE only). The GroupPermissionEvaluator javadoc for canManage() ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") encodes the same mistake and should be corrected too. No test covers a VIEW-only all-groups permission attempting to create a group.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes/returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In V2 a per-group Resource is created with name == group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource) and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves it with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() however calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) with the authz resource UUID and then adds groupResource.getId() to the result set. Consequences: (1) findByName with a resource UUID never matches, so the code always falls back to the all-groups resource, meaning per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are never detected and an all-groups permission is reported for every iterated resource; (2) the returned set contains resource UUIDs, but callers (UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) feed it into session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) and getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds), which expect group IDs, so user search/count return nothing. Both places should use groupResource.getName() and skip the "Groups" placeholder resource itself. Note also that getOrCreateResource never calls setType(resourceType) on the per-group resource, so findByType(server, "Groups") currently only returns the placeholder resource created in init(), making this method effectively dead for real groups and leaving GET /users/count wrong for admins with only group-member permissions.

findings.title: Existence of any per-group permission disables the all-groups fallback for that group
findings.body: hasPermission() only consults the Groups resource-type resource when no specific resource named by the group id exists. Once a specific resource exists for a group (e.g. because someone granted VIEW_MEMBERS on it), evaluation is done only against that resource and the requested scopes; if the specific permission does not include the requested scope (e.g. VIEW/MANAGE) the method returns false even though the caller holds an all-groups permission granting that scope. So granting a narrow per-group permission silently revokes broader type-level rights for that group (e.g. canView(group) becomes false for an admin with view-all-groups). The method should fall back to the type-level resource when the specific-resource evaluation does not grant the scope, or evaluate both.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong predicate
findings.body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementations (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) check canManageMembers(GroupModel). The two scopes (manage-members vs manage-membership) have different meanings, so the doc misleads callers about which permission is enforced. Also, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's @return says "Stream of IDs" while the method returns a Set.

findings.title: No cleanup of V2 group resources/permissions when a group is removed
findings.body: The ProviderEventListener that reacts to GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent is registered only when the V1 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is enabled, and even then it calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false), which GroupPermissionsV2 implements by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. With this PR, V2 now creates per-group authz Resources (named by group id) and scope permissions referencing them, but nothing removes them when the group is deleted. Deleted groups therefore leave orphaned Resource/Policy rows in the admin-permissions resource server that keep showing up in permission listings and in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/findByType iterations.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() maps Users resources to a human-readable name ("All users" or the username) but falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Group resources created by getOrCreateResource() have name == group id and no display name set, so for Groups-type permissions this returns null (and the "Groups" placeholder gets no "All groups" label). Any consumer that relies on this method (e.g. admin UI permission listings) will show empty names for group permissions. A Groups branch resolving the group and returning its name/path, plus an "All groups" label, is needed for parity with Users.

findings.title: MANAGE_MEMBERS cannot be used to create users in V2 because canCreateGroupMembers is gated on the V1 feature flag
findings.body: canCreateGroupMembers() returns false unless Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. V1 and V2 are versions of the same feature and cannot be enabled together, so under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 the newly added Groups MANAGE_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes are never consulted when creating a user with `groups` in the representation; createUser() always fails with 403 unless the admin has the manage-users role or an all-users MANAGE permission. Either the gate should also accept V2 or the limitation should be documented.

findings.title: Missing negative/edge coverage for new group scopes
findings.body: The new test class only exercises happy paths for the Groups scopes. Not covered: (a) that an all-groups VIEW permission does NOT allow creating a top-level group (which would catch the canManage() VIEW bug); (b) that joining a group requires the group-level MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission (testManageGroupMembership grants both all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and the group permission at once, so a missing group check would not be detected); (c) GET /groups/{id}/members with VIEW_MEMBERS; (d) GET /users/count for an admin with only group VIEW_MEMBERS permissions (which exercises getGroupIdsWithViewPermission and would expose the resource-id vs group-id bug); (e) a group with a specific narrow permission plus an all-groups VIEW permission (fallback behaviour).

findings.title: Per-subgroup policy evaluation before pagination in V2
findings.body: getSubGroups() loads all subgroups (getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)) and filters with auth.groups()::canView before paginating. In V2, canView(GroupModel) does not short-circuit on a global permission: each call does a resource lookup, a policyStore.findByResource on the type resource and a full policy evaluation. For an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission on a parent with thousands of children this results in thousands of policy evaluations per page request (same pattern in GroupsResource.getGroups). The previous code evaluated the global check once (canViewGlobal); if per-group negative permissions must be honoured, consider at least caching the all-groups evaluation result within the evaluator instance for the request.
